issues.description: The problem description lists attribute names 'inscribedStudents' and 'guestStudents' (problem_statement.md lines 16-18), but the UML diagram and the provided solution/template use 'numberOfInscribedStudents' and 'numberOfGuestStudents' (problem_statement.md UML lines 63-68 and solution/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java lines 6-10). This naming inconsistency between the prose and the UML/solution may confuse students about the exact attribute names they should implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the attribute names consistent across the problem text, UML diagram, template, and solution. Update the prose in problem_statement.md to reference 'numberOfInscribedStudents' and 'numberOfGuestStudents' (or alternatively change the UML and solution to use 'inscribedStudents' and 'guestStudents') so students have a single, unambiguous set of attribute names to implement.

issues.description: The problem statement prose refers to the student-count attributes as 'inscribedStudents' and 'guestStudents' (lines 16-18), whereas the UML, tests and the solution implementation use 'numberOfInscribedStudents' and 'numberOfGuestStudents' (UML lines 63-69 and solution attributes lines 6-10). This creates a naming mismatch that can confuse students when mapping the textual requirements to the expected attribute names and getters/setters in the code and tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the problem statement wording with the UML and solution by using the explicit attribute names 'numberOfInscribedStudents' and 'numberOfGuestStudents' in the prose (and any task descriptions). Also update the template TODO/comments to mention the exact attribute names expected, so students can map requirements to implementation and tests without ambiguity.
